brief: brief-js162.md with js162-measurements.md: helpers end to end in jellyfin-web on 2-CPU workers (one run per configuration, 5 minutes after the seek, a shared local directory). As built, two equal workers play a 4K HDR re-encode exactly as one does (no helper ever starts; 302 to 304 refusals per play for the room kept for a new viewer, with one viewer and nothing queued); three hold real time until a seek, then 0.72 to 0.84x because the helper left behind runs on unbounded (5 min 25 s, to the film's end in another run); a 2-CPU and a 6-CPU worker play it only if the job lands on the large one (it landed on the small one in 2 of 2 first plays). With the room rule lifted: three workers real time throughout, two until the seek, small plus large throughout. Options A (keep), B (bound a helper by its viewers), C (drop the room rule), D (place the job on the worker that holds it), B with C.
tradeoff: Whether room held empty for a viewer who has not asked is worth a film stalling beside an idle worker; and, once helpers may fill every worker, who gives way when a second viewer arrives: the viewer already watching (their helpers stopped, a stall) or the newcomer (a refusal with its reason).
entry: A is rejected. B is JS-167 at 15 (a helper no viewer's place bounds stops within 5 seconds). C is JS-168 at 16 (no room is held back for a viewer who has not asked; two equal workers must hold the film before and after a seek, three runs, which also proves B with C; a second viewer's arrival is observed there). D is JS-161's placement criterion made exact (10 of 10 plays on the worker that holds the job). JS-161 moves to 17, depends on both and gains two rules, because as written it would refuse every play JS-162 saw helpers carry (those workers were counted 3.2 cores by the floor it removes): a play no one worker holds but the workers with room hold together is admitted; and a viewer watching at real time is never taken under it by a newcomer, so, as a default that JS-168's second-viewer figures confirm or change by a brief before JS-161's Spec, a helper of a job its own worker does not hold at 1.2 times real time alone is held as that play's own and the newcomer is refused with its reason and counted as demand. Given up: on a cluster one shared film fills, a second viewer is refused where today they would start, by the second viewer; the server's own held-back room, by nobody (the operator's sizing and the autoscaler's target keep it, D-048). JS-166 depends on JS-161, JS-167 and JS-168 and moves ahead of JS-164. JS-162 closes with its deviation recorded; BL-242 is promoted; BL-245 holds the two unexplained slow runs. Rejected: narrower forms of the room rule (unmeasured, and the room is better kept where no playing film pays for it); a second viewer stopping the helpers a first one needs (a stall for someone who was watching, with no reason shown). Unverified when decided: B alone after a seek, B with C on two workers, the second viewer's start in seconds, any store between machines, other processors; each is an acceptance criterion. Data that reopens it: JS-168 showing two workers do not hold the film after a seek; the dogfood's count of refusals made while a helper held the cores.
serves: PRODUCT.md: 'Play starts in seconds and keeps up. A heavy film uses the whole cluster's processors rather than stalling on one machine while others sit idle.' Goal 1: 'Playback never surprises a viewer. Starting, seeking, resuming, and recovering from a failure just work, for every film.' 'every failure is reported with its reason, never silent'.
